text:
Andrea: Heads up, perf regression after yesterday's canary. nsys shows one kernel dominating GPU time; suspect KV eviction + batching heuristic change.
Mike: which kernel and what are the numbers?
Andrea: top stack is a softmax-related kernel (softmax_backward_cuda / fused-softmax). nsys summary clipped from the trace: 

% Total GPU Time | Kernel                         | Calls | Avg (ms)
----------------------------------------------------------------
  48.7%           softmax_backward_cuda            140    1.18
  19.3%           attention_kv_update              600    0.28
  11.1%           layernorm_backward              1200   0.10
   8.9%           quant_matmul                     70    1.92

Andrea: baseline before deploy was ~0.16-0.2ms for that softmax kernel; canary shows ~1.1-1.3ms. Also seeing lower achieved occupancy and spikes in issue-stalled cycles during the kernel.
Sana: what capture command and runtime flags? was prefetch forced on/off? batch sizes?
Andrea: ran on p4d with: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o perf_canary.nsys python run_infer.py --batch 4 --kv-prefetch=auto`
Andrea: deploy changes: batcher window reduced 50ms -> 20ms, per-GPU KV cache capacity decreased by ~25%, and default prefetch mode moved to 'auto' in config.
Mike: auto prefetch + smaller cache smells like eviction churn. If KV pages are evicted more often, we rebuild KV and subsequent attention/softmax work increases due to longer effective seq lengths and additional memory traffic.
perf-ci-bot: Trace uploaded: https://internal-ci/redwood/nsys/1747771234/perf_canary.nsys :thumbsup:
Sana: can you pull sm_efficiency / warp_serialize / issue_stalled counters from the nsys timeline and paste quick stats? want to see divergence vs baseline.
Andrea: quick counters from nsys stats (canary vs baseline):
- sm_efficiency: canary 42% vs baseline 78%
- warp_serialize: canary 9.2% vs baseline 1.1%
- achieved_occupancy: canary 0.62 vs baseline 0.91
Andrea: perfetto timeline shows clusters of H2D transfers coincident with attention_kv_update gaps, likely KV rebuild traffic.
Mike: repro plan: run small A/B: (1) kv-cache capacity revert + batcher window 50ms + kv-prefetch=on; (2) current canary settings; (3) kv-prefetch=off variants; capture nsys for each and compare top kernels and counters. Also try batch sizes 1,4,8 to see batching behavior.
Sana: I'll spin up a reproduce matrix on a spare p4d. will capture `nsys stats` and small nvprof samples for occupancy counters.
Andrea: did a quick local smoke:
- canary (reduced cache, window 20ms): softmax avg 1.18ms, total GPU time 48.7%
- revert cache + window 50ms + kv-prefetch=on: softmax avg 0.19ms, total GPU time 6.9%
So numbers snap back when cache restored.
Sherman: if that reproduces on canary infra, I'll roll back KV-cache config for the affected pool. Keep me posted with the compare traces.
Mike: if confirmed, add a perf regression test: synthetic micro-benchmark that asserts softmax p50/p95 under varied batch windows and cache sizes. Also add a sliding-window alert on kernel time regression for critical kernels.
Sana: will attach compare traces here once jobs finish and include a small perf script that extracts top-kernels and sm counters (`nsys stats --report gputrace perf_canary.nsys`). Also will test `--batch 1` to reproduce cold-start and eviction scenarios.
Andrea: one more theory: kernel variant selection could flip (vectorized vs scalar softmax) depending on input alignment when KV rebuild changes the tensor layout. Need kernel team to check whether small input alignment shifts could force slower code paths.
Mike: good call. If traces show a different kernel name or params in the stack, open an audit ticket for kernel selection heuristics.
Andrea: TL;DR: softmax-related kernel latency regressed ~6x in canary. Evidence points to KV-cache eviction thrash combined with narrower batch window and 'auto' prefetch. Action items: reproduce traces with cache revert, test prefetch toggles, add regression test, and engage kernel team if variant selection changes present.
Sherman: ack. I'll prepare rollback plan pending the compare traces.
